21.title: Implement validated atomic inventory file library
21.body:
Implements Issue #6: other Python programs can load, validate and atomically save format-v1 inventory documents. Invalid content and duplicate IDs are rejected before modifying a destination. Extra fields and repeated JSON keys are rejected; the README documents the API and its atomic-replacement boundary.

Spec pin: Issue #6, spec_sha256=05254ec36c91071580cc72e49527a36f4403b403712cf7aaba26873a996bb9f2, acceptance https://github.com/fixture/receipt-desk/issues/6#issuecomment-1.

Candidate: 5331b0bbab3ece9e94ddac3fe24def2ddf7a2180; base b66b48cc9e28e9d17639406a17bc609ff80b2a9a. Exact candidate is available on local shared/codex/inventory-library (verified using git ls-remote).

Validation on Python 3.14.2:
- python3 -m unittest discover -s tests: 11 tests passed, including invalid documents, exact-byte preservation, replacement boundary and failure cleanup.
- python3 .agents/corp/check.py --base b66b48cc9e28e9d17639406a17bc609ff80b2a9a: passed; local route/helper/diff evidence only.
- A separate caller imported inventory, loaded inputs/inventory.csv, saved and reloaded both records, then attempted a duplicate-ID save and verified unchanged old bytes: passed.

Known limits: no writer locking or power-loss durability promise. No independent review, CI run, main integration or formal stage acceptance has occurred. This is an offline fixture PR and local bare-Git publication, not real GitHub publication. Issue #8 remains contributor-command work; its README premise has changed from example-only tests to real library tests. Issue #9 remains supplied-example diagnostics work.

Successor: recover Issue #6 checkpoint and this exact branch; run the documented checks and the generated development loop to organize any applicable independent stage review. The implementer has not reviewed their own candidate independently.
